purpose: Causal functional attribution of completed P training; not a new claimed paper method or another mean-calibration fit
hypothesis: Determine whether shared token-function drift is sufficient for SSIM gains and whether sample-dependent drift retains useful stimulus evidence after that shared drift is removed
selection_basis: The original positive-only reference and preregistered joint P objective, both retained. No search among nine cases and no IP-to-P parameter-matched claim.

T.subject: sub-03
T.source: Genuine native OOF c followed by the same frozen matching ordinary; whole ordinary head has seen T

mean_scope: All T only, no evaluation target/label/image/score. Four token slots retain distinct 2048D shifts; not a shared-token-bias softmax invariant.
precision: Original FP16 A/P inference; T mean from FP64 sums of actual FP16 tokens, then FP32 mean. New tokens rounded once to FP16 and measured. This intervention changes LN output geometry and is not claimed to preserve token norms or output distribution.
controls_reused: Exact completed v303 full830 images and features; no reference image reruns except two engineering parity images
fixed_comparisons: Each new intervention minus matching ordinary and its own full trained P
Common versus specific for each P case

generation.noise: Exact previous per-query initial and all ancestral RNG draws

metrics: All14 previous readings: DINO, original paper7 and EffNet; exact same evaluators. ObjectF1/CapSim still absent, no fabricated SEED.

bootstrap.interpretation: Descriptive, exposed development set, fixed comparisons, no multiplicity-adjusted confirmation

prior_art_boundary: Classical mean/residual intervention, related to earlier mean controls. New question is loss-induced functional drift in these actual trained native P checkpoints, with complementary components and nonlinear full-image interaction. No originality or SOTA claimed.
